headline: Ten-man US beat Bosnia 2-0 to reach World Cup round of 16 after Balogun red card
summary: The United States secured their spot in the World Cup round of 16 with a 2-0 victory over Bosnia, despite playing with 10 men for part of the match after Folarin Balogun received a red card.
details: The United States advanced to the World Cup round of 16 after a 2-0 win against Bosnia on Wednesday. Malik Tillman scored from a free kick, securing the victory for the 10-man co-hosts.
Folarin Balogun had opened the scoring in the first half but was later sent off for a heavy challenge on Tarik Muharemovic. The decision was confirmed after a Video Assistant Referee (VAR) review.

Balogun's initial goal came in the 45th minute, capitalizing on a deflection off Muharemovic to slip a left-foot shot under the goalkeeper's legs. Tillman then doubled the US's lead in the 82nd minute.
This marks the first time the US has won a knockout match at a World Cup since their run to the quarter-finals in 2002. The team showed resilience to secure the win despite being a man down.
The co-hosts are now set to face Belgium in the next stage of the tournament. They will compete for a place in the quarter-finals, continuing their World Cup journey.

headline: Torch procession in 5 districts demands Teesta Master Plan approval by ECNEC
summary: Residents across five districts have taken to the streets with torches, urging the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) to approve the long-awaited Teesta Master Plan.
details: A torch procession was held across five districts in Bangladesh, with participants demanding the immediate approval of the Teesta Master Plan by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC). The demonstration underscores the growing public urgency for the project.

The proposed Teesta Master Plan aims to address critical issues such as riverbank erosion, flood control, and irrigation, which are vital for the agricultural economy and livelihoods of millions in the northern region.

Local communities and activists have long advocated for the implementation of this comprehensive plan, viewing it as essential for sustainable development and improved water management along the Teesta River.

ECNEC, the highest body for approving public sector projects in Bangladesh, is expected to review the plan. Its approval is seen as a crucial step towards securing necessary funding and commencing the extensive development work.
